newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK airline blocks exiled Cambodian prince's return.
newsitem.headline: HK airline blocks exiled Cambodian prince's return.

text.p: Hong Kong airline Dragonair blocked a bid by Cambodia's exiled Prince Norodom Sirivudh to fly home to Phnom Penh on Tuesday after being told by the government there that he was not welcome.
"Dragonair really has no alternative but to deny him boarding. He will not be allowed to board the flight," Dragonair spokesman John Bailey told Reuters.

"The position now is that Dragonair has been notified officially by the Cambodian government that Prince Norodom (Sirivudh) will not be welcomed into Cambodia and he will not be allowed to enter Cambodia," Bailey said.

Sirivudh, former foreign minister and half brother of King Norodom Sihanouk, went into exile in December 1995 after being held for one month on charges of involvement in an alleged plot against the life of Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.
The exiled prince has denied the charges and has said he wants to return to seek justice.
But Hun Sen has warned of possible dire consequences if Sirivudh returns.
In Phnom Penh earlier on Tuesday, co-Interior Minister You Hockry said Sirivudh would be taken to prison if he returned.
"If he arrives he will be taken to T3 (prison in Phnom Penh). That's what we plan to do," he said.
The prince, who arrived in Hong Kong from Frankfurt on Tuesday, was told by Dragonair he would not be allowed to board, despite having a reservation.
"He's already been told that. He's actually in the transit lounge so he has been approached by Dragonair officials and informed of the situation," Bailey said.
He also said Cambodian consular officials in Hong Kong had arrived at the airport earlier and notified Dragonair of Phnom Penh's decision.
Sirivudh, in a transit lounge at the airport, would be staying in Hong Kong for the next few days, an aide of the prince told Reuters by telephone.
The aide also said the prince was determined to fly home. "Phnom Penh, for sure," the aide said when asked where the prince's next destination would be.
Sirivudh was attempting to organise a news conference at the airport as soon as he was through immigration.
